title: [BugFix][Quantization] Release ModelSlim MoE reload metadata references
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The ModelSlim MoE loader wrapper closes over a bound method, retaining its layer through vLLM reload metadata. Return a method bound to the owning layer so the existing reload sanitizer can break that reference; preserve the plain-callable path and weight-name mapping.

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/18679

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Discarded MoE layers and their weight tensors can be collected after reload metadata is recorded. Weight-name mapping, forwarded arguments and loader return values are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- Tested vLLM-Ascend main source at `33dd6e797de414db6981ec4afb09ab71baaddd60`, with its CI-pinned vLLM source `c4df37dfcc7f72ca41cd43801a468526ecf99a2b`.
- `tests/ut/quantization/configs/test_modelslim_config.py`: **72 passed and 15 subtests passed**. Restoring the baseline production file makes both new ownership/lifetime regressions fail (**2 failed**). The lifetime case records actual vLLM reload metadata and checks layer and weight weak references after collection.
- Command, from the relevant checkout in the repository CPU UT environment:

```sh
/work/.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/ut tests/ut/quantization/configs/test_modelslim_config.py -q
```

- Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu, pytest 9.1.1. CPU dependencies came from `quay.nju.edu.cn/ascend/vllm-omni:v0.30.0`; the checked-out sources above were used, not the image's framework source.
- `bash format.sh ci`: passed, including the secret scan and shell checks.
- mypy 1.11.1 on the changed runtime module and regression test (checked as separate targets): Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 targets passed. The plain-callable wrapper and the fixture use distinct names to avoid `no-redef` errors.
- The same CPU suite was rerun after that correction: 72 passed and 15 subtests passed. The local type-check environment used NumPy 2.2.6.
- Replaying the CI rebase command locally succeeds and produces exactly the reviewed source tree.
- The repository CPU UT mocks were used and no NPU devices were mounted. NPU/model/E2E execution and upstream CI have not been validated by this local run. Hardware checks remain required before merge where applicable.
- AI assistance was used to prepare the change and validation.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: reviewed applicable boundaries and preserved existing compatibility coverage.
- [x] **Regression test**: included a regression that fails on the baseline.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: no additional device-failure coverage is claimed.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: CPU scope and remaining hardware checks are stated above.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: no NPU performance benchmark was run or claimed.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542
